Hayden School District NO. RE-1 Ballot Issue 4A
SHALL THE HAYDEN SCHOOL DISTRICT RE-1 TAXES BE INCREASED BY THE AMOUNT OF $525,861 IN BUDGET YEAR 2026-2027, AND AN AMOUNT TO BE DETERMINED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER BY IMPOSING A PROPERTY TAX LEVY EITHER AT A RATE SUFFICIENT TO PRODUCE THE AMOUNT SPECIFIED ABOVE, OR AT A RATE OF 3.0 MILLS, WHICHEVER WILL PRODUCE THE HIGHEST TAX REVENUES IN THE GIVEN TAX COLLECTION YEAR, FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES TO BE APPROVED BY THE BOARD OF EDUCATION WHICH SHALL INCLUDE, BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO FUNDING COSTS NECESSARY FOR MAINTAINING SMALL CLASS SIZES, ATTRACTING AND RETAINING HIGHLY QUALIFIED TEACHERS AND STAFF, AND TO PROVIDE ADEQUATE MAINTENANCE, UPGRADES, AND RENOVATION OF FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT, BY COLLECTING, DEPOSITING INTO THE GENERAL FUND, RETAINING AND EXPENDING ALL REVENUES DERIVED FROM SUCH TAX, WHICH SHALL BE INDEPENDENT OF ANY OTHER TAX LEVY WHETHER OR NOT APPROVED BY THE VOTERS, AND ANY EARNINGS FROM THE INVESTMENT THEREOF, AS A VOTER APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE AND AN EXCEPTION TO LIMITS WHICH WOULD OTHERWISE APPLY UNDER ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION OR ANY OTHER LAW?

Hayden School District NO. RE-1 Ballot Issue 4B
SHALL THE PROPERTY WITHIN THE BOUNDARIES OF HAYDEN SCHOOL DISTRICT RE-1 BE INCLUDED WITHIN THE BOUNDARIES OF THE COLORADO MOUNTAIN COLLEGE DISTRICT, AND SHALL TAXABLE PROPERTY WITHIN HAYDEN SCHOOL DISTRICT RE-1 BE SUBJECT TO THE MILL LEVY IMPOSED BY THE COLORADO MOUNTAIN COLLEGE DISTRICT (CURRENTLY 3.82 MILLS, SUBJECT TO CHANGE BASED ON COLORADO MOUNTAIN COLLEGE DISTRICT FUTURE YEARLY CERTIFICATIONS) ON THE SAME BASIS AS OTHER PROPERTY LOCATED WITHIN THE COLORADO MOUNTAIN COLLEGE DISTRICT, AND IN SO DOING EXPAND THE AVAILABILITY OF LOW COST COLLEGE DEGREES AND CERTIFICATES; CONTINUING EDUCATION AND LIFELONG LEARNING; TUITION FREE CONCURRENT ENROLLMENT FOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS; AND SKILLED TRADES AND INDUSTRY-SPECIFIC TRAINING, ON BEHALF OF THE RESIDENTS OF HAYDEN SCHOOL DISTRICT RE-1?

West Routt Fire Protection District Ballot Issue 6A
SHALL WEST ROUTT FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICT TAXES BE INCREASED $448,950.00 (FIRST FULL FISCAL YEAR DOLLAR INCREASE) BEGINNING IN LEVY YEAR 2027 (FOR COLLECTION IN CALENDAR YEAR 2028), AND BY SUCH ADDITIONAL AMOUNTS AS ARE COLLECTED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER THROUGH THE IMPOSITION OF AN ADDITIONAL MILL LEVY OF NOT TO EXCEED 3.0 MILLS WITH THE REVENUE FROM THE INCREASE TO BE USED FOR THE PURPOSE OF MAINTAINING AND IMPROVING THE DISTRICT'S LEVELS OF SERVICE, INCLUDING:
• SUPPORTING ITS EMERGENCY MEDICAL AND TRANSPORTATION SERVICES AND ITS FIREFIGHTING SERVICES;
• HIRING AND RETAINING PERSONNEL, INCLUDING EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS, FIREFIGHTERS AND OTHER EMERGENCY SERVICE PROFESSIONS, AND
• PROVIDING NECESSARY EQUIPMENT FOR EMTS AND FIREFIGHTERS, AND PAYING THE COSTS OF OPERATIONS AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE DISTRICT,
AND SHALL THE WEST ROUTT FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICT BE AUTHORIZED TO COLLECT, RETAIN, AND SPEND ALL REVENUES FROM SUCH TAX AS A VOTER APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE UNDER ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION?

Town of Oak Creek Ballot Issue 2A
SHALL THE TOWN OF OAK CREEK TAXES BE INCREASED $400,000 ANNUALLY, COMMENCING JANUARY 1, 2027, AND BY WHATEVER ADDITIONAL AMOUNTS ARE RAISED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER, FROM A SALES TAX RATE INCREASE OF 2.00% (WHICH REPRESENTS A TWO CENT INCREASE ON EACH DOLLAR) TO BE SPENT AS A VOTER-APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE WITH 100% OF THE REVENUES FROM THE SALES TAX RATE INCREASE TO BE DEPOSITED INTO THE GENERAL FUND AND EXPENDED SOLELY FOR THE CONSTRUCTION AND REHABILITATION OF CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS; AND SHALL ALL TAX REVENUES DEPOSITED IN SAID FUND AND ALL EARNINGS THEREON (REGARDLESS OF AMOUNT) CONSTITUTE A VOTER APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE AND AN EXCEPTION TO THE REVENUE AND SPENDING LIMITS OF ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION?

Morrison Creek Metropolitan Water & Sanitation District Ballot Issue 6B
SHALL THE MORRISON CREEK METROPOLITAN WATER AND SANITATION DISTRICT (THE "DISTRICT") WAIVE THE 5.25% PROPERTY TAX LIMIT FOR ALL FUTURE PROPERTY TAX YEARS, AS SUCH PROPERTY TAX LIMIT IS SET FORTH IN SECTION 29-1-1702, C.R.S., PROVIDED HOWEVER THAT THE ADJUSTED PROPERTY TAX MILL LEVY OF THE DISTRICT FOR EACH FISCAL YEAR OF 2027 THROUGH 2031 SHALL BE EQUAL TO THE ADJUSTED PROPERTY TAX MILL LEVY IMPOSED BY THE DISTRICT IN 2026 (THE FOREGOING WAIVER BEING PROVIDED FOR AND PERMITTED BY SECTION 29-1-1704, C.R.S.), AND SHALL THE DISTRICT BE AUTHORIZED TO COLLECT, RETAIN, AND SPEND THE FULL AMOUNT OF ALL PROPERTY TAX MILL LEVY REVENUES IMPOSED, GENERATED, COLLECTED OR RECEIVED BY THE DISTRICT DURING 2026 AND EACH FISCAL YEAR THEREAFTER, SUCH AMOUNTS AND REVENUES TO CONSTITUTE A VOTER APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE, AND SHALL THE DISTRICT BE AUTHORIZED TO INCREASE THE TOTAL NUMBER OF MILLS LEVIED BY THE DISTRICT IN EACH FUTURE PROPERTY TAX YEAR TO A MAXIMUM OF 20 MILLS AS PERMITTED BY SECTION 29-1-1705(2)(a), C.R.S., AND SHALL THE PROPERTY TAX MILL LEVY REVENUES AS MAY BE IMPOSED, GENERATED, COLLECTED, RETAINED AND SPENT BY THE DISTRICT IN ALL FUTURE PROPERTY TAX YEARS BE WITHOUT REGARD TO ANY SPENDING, REVENUE RAISING, OR OTHER LIMITATION CONTAINED IN ARTICLE X, SECTION 20, OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION, AND WITHOUT REGARD TO ANY LIMITS IMPOSED ON INCREASES IN PROPERTY TAXATION OR REVENUES BY SECTION 29-1-301, C.R.S., AND BY SECTION 29-1-1702, C.R.S., IN ANY SUBSEQUENT PROPERTY TAX YEAR, AND WITHOUT REGARD TO ANY OTHER LAW WHICH PURPORTS TO LIMIT THE DISTRICT'S PROPERTY TAX REVENUES OR EXPENDITURES OR NUMBER OF MILLS LEVIED AS CURRENTLY EXISTS OR AS MAY BE AMENDED OR ADDED IN THE FUTURE?

Yampa Valley Regional Transportation Authority Ballot Issue 7A
SHALL YAMPA VALLEY REGIONAL TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (RTA) TAXES BE INCREASED BY $7,875,197.00 ANNUALLY, BEGINNING IN THE FIRST FULL FISCAL YEAR, AND BY WHATEVER ADDITIONAL AMOUNTS ARE RAISED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER, BY IMPOSING, BEGINNING JANUARY 1, 2027, A SALES TAX AT A RATE OF ONE-HALF OF ONE PERCENT, EQUIVALENT TO FIFTY CENTS ON EACH ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS OF TAXABLE PURCHASES, UPON EVERY TRANSACTION OR OTHER INCIDENT WITH RESPECT TO WHICH A SALES TAX IS LEVIED BY THE STATE, SUBJECT TO THE SAME EXEMPTIONS THAT APPLY TO THE STATE SALES TAX, FOR THE FOLLOWING PURPOSES:
• ENHANCING PUBLIC SAFETY ON HIGHWAY 40, DECREASING THE RISK OF ACCIDENTS, AND PROVIDING SAFER ALTERNATIVES FOR RESIDENTS AND WORKERS TRAVELING BETWEEN COMMUNITIES
• IMPROVING TRANSPORTATION OPTIONS FOR LOCAL WORKERS, RESIDENTS, SENIORS, AND VISITORS ACROSS THE YAMPA VALLEY
• PARTICIPATING IN REGIONAL PLANNING FOR FUTURE COMMUTER RAIL SERVICE BETWEEN CRAIG, HAYDEN, STEAMBOAT SPRINGS, OAK CREEK, AND YAMPA
• PROVIDING AFFORDABLE REGIONAL TRANSPORTATION OPTIONS TO AREAS THAT ARE NOT CURRENTLY SERVED BY TRANSIT
AND SHALL THE YAMPA VALLEY REGIONAL TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (RTA) BE AUTHORIZED TO COLLECT, RETAIN, AND SPEND ALL REVENUES FROM SUCH TAX AS A VOTER-APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE ABOVE THE ANNUAL LIMITS OF ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION?
